question: Perth, early 1980s. Stomach ulcers heal on acid-blocking pills, then come back. What really causes most of them?
answer: A bacterium, Helicobacter pylori. It grew in the lab only in 1982, when Easter left a plate in the incubator for five days instead of the usual two. Barry Marshall drinking a culture made headlines but proved little. The trials did: kill the germ and the ulcers stop returning. Nobel Prize, 2005.
move: A treatment that works only while you take it may be hiding the cause.
ask: What problem in my life do I keep treating without ever asking what causes it?

clues.text: Ulcers heal while patients take acid-blocking pills; most return when they stop.
Curved bacteria turn up in the stomach lining of nearly every ulcer patient.
A doctor drinks a flask of the bacteria. Within days his stomach is inflamed.
After two weeks of antibiotics, ulcers stay healed. Stress and acid are unchanged.

scene.why: The drink gave inflammation, not an ulcer. The cure decided: kill the germ, and ulcers stay away.

reference: Marshall, Helicobacter connections, Nobel Lecture, Nobel Foundation, 2005
